A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same context-bias study despite substantial revision. Text, equations, tables and figures support comparison. v2's supplementary material, including its duplicated supplementary copy, was checked; v3 ends with references and contains no separate appendix.

before.justification: v2 reports original detector evaluations, background-suppression experiments, feature-distribution analyses and a MIC augmentation ablation, with extensive supplementary results.

after.justification: v3 reports original background-replacement and feature-suppression experiments, detector evaluations, and gradient and feature-discrepancy analyses in Tables 3–9.

M1.justification: v3 introduces grouping instances and features by whether detection survives background removal, then computing domain association gradients and associated/non-associated feature contrasts. v2 computes general foreground/background MMD and MVD without these groups. This substantially changes the proposed quantification procedure, beyond expanding its explanation.

E1.justification: v3 adds rainy Cityscapes and randomized-background scenarios using BG-20K. Virtual KITTI weather variants were already evaluated in v2 Table 18, but its viewpoint variants disappear. CARLA remains in motivating examples while its systematic training and cross-domain analyses are removed, substantially changing coverage.

E2.justification: EfficientNet-B0-FPN is added as an evaluated comparator, while v2's MIC-augmented Detectron2 comparison disappears. ALDI++, already evaluated through association graphs in v2, additionally participates in v3's quantitative performance and perturbation comparisons. These changes substantially reshape the evaluated comparison set.

E3.justification: Reported settings change substantially: the ResNet learning rate changes from 0.015 to 0.02, KITTI image resolution from 618×2048 to 375×1242, and YOLO batch size from 15 to 8. v3 also introduces controlled background sampling and gradient-based evaluation while dropping MVD. These are revised or additional protocols, not evidence of comparable-setting performance gains.

E4.justification: v3 adds randomized-background controls, quantitative detection-drop analysis across CAM thresholds, and associated/non-associated feature comparisons. Background suppression itself already existed in v2. Conversely, v2's MIC mitigation ablation, size-stratified MMD analyses and supplementary embedding case studies are removed.

E5.justification: v2 provides heat-ratio means and standard deviations and MMD distribution plots, without an explicit repeated-evaluation or significance-testing protocol. v3 newly reports six evaluation repetitions, mAP mean±SD, Wilcoxon tests, Shapiro-Wilk checks and pairwise t-tests, with significance annotations. Six independent model-training runs are not established.

E6.justification: v3 Tables 3–9 introduce substantial performance, randomized-background, drop-rate and gradient results, while v2's MIC and detailed MVD results disappear. For example, Cityscapes-trained Detectron2 reports foggy-validation AP50 of 46.321 in v2 Table 13, whereas v3 Table 3 reports 57.13 for Res. Changed training settings prevent interpreting this as a same-setting gain.

T1.justification: v3 expands v2's probability-factorization discussion into a causal framework with a PC-algorithm graph, an explicit foreground/background independence assumption, association variable A and backdoor intervention formula. Equations 3–6 add formal domain-gradient and associated/non-associated MMD definitions. These are substantive mathematical additions, rather than notation changes.

C1.justification: v2 emphasizes empirical context-bias quantification and reports improved accuracy from MIC-style augmentation. v3 removes that mitigation claim and centers its contributions on causal identification and a novel domain association gradient. Its abstract and conclusion now explicitly claim that context bias causally undermines cross-domain generalization.

C2.justification: v3 adds causal interpretations of interventions and gradient comparisons, explanations for anomalous EfficientNet outcomes, and limitations involving class imbalance, transformers and CAM compatibility. Unlike v2's YOLO feature analyses, v3 excludes YOLO from Q2/Q3 because of its stated NMS differentiation limitation. The computational-cost limitation is retained.

D1.justification: Reproducibility documentation is substantially revised. v3 specifies target-performance-based checkpoint selection, pretrained ALDI++ handling, RTX A4500 hardware, a 0.85 CAM confidence threshold and model-specific extraction layers. It omits v2's explicit scheduler milestones, several optimizer settings and per-class instance-count tables. Newly disclosed details alone do not establish underlying procedural changes.

R1.justification: v3 substantially strengthens positioning around causal discovery and representation learning, adding works such as Glymour et al. and Schölkopf et al., alongside background-masking and statistical references. It drops several earlier references, including the MMD and MVD sources, and reframes novelty around causal analysis rather than primarily empirical discrepancy measurement.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Earlier method and visualization material moves into an expanded introduction, and methods and experiments are reorganized around Q1–Q3. Terminology, abbreviations, algorithm descriptions and citation style are also revised; this exceeds changes caused solely by adding experiments.

P2.justification: v3 changes the document from two columns to one, restructures results into comparative tables, redraws association displays, and adds causal and feature-extraction diagrams plus significance-annotated box plots. Numerous supplementary matrices, violin plots and embeddings disappear. Some motivating figures and UMAP content are retained or rearranged.

improvement.justification: v3 adds useful randomized-background controls, repeated evaluations, uncertainty reporting and explicit applicability limits, but removes v2's direct MIC mitigation ablation. Its central new gradient analysis also contains an unresolved contradiction: Section 3.6 predicts GradientS > GradientT, whereas Q3-Exp1 predicts the reverse and interprets Table 8 as support. Because this affects the meaning of a principal new contribution, the empirical gains and interpretive problems do not permit a reliable net quality judgment.
